subject.title: [Feature]: Move away from useMultiFileAuthState for Baileys

question: Should the WhatsApp plugin adopt plugin-owned SQLite as its sole canonical Baileys auth-state store, and what migration, backup, rollback, and legacy-file deletion contract must it guarantee?
rationale: This changes sensitive shipped session storage and upgrade behavior; source inspection establishes the need but cannot choose the permanent database lifecycle or acceptable re-pair/data-loss boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve SQLite migration
options.body: Adopt a plugin-owned SQLite schema, migrate and verify existing Baileys files once, then remove legacy files and run only the canonical database path.

options.title: Retain hardened files
options.body: Keep multi-file auth temporarily and limit work to additional atomicity, diagnostics, and recovery hardening while documenting the production caveat.

options.title: Sponsor another backend
options.body: Define a different supported storage contract only if SQLite cannot satisfy the plugin’s transaction, portability, or lifecycle requirements.

recommendation.title: Approve SQLite migration
recommendation.body: Adopt a plugin-owned SQLite schema, migrate and verify existing Baileys files once, then remove legacy files and run only the canonical database path.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent auth-state stabilization and persistence work is the closest historical ownership signal for deciding the migration boundary.
